images.title: Collecting half rotis
images.purpose: Show one half roti as a unit that is added again and again: 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/2 = 3 × 1/2, which is 1 full roti and 1/2 more.
images.composition: Three groups in one row with wide gaps: one half roti alone, three half rotis in a row, then one full roti with one half beside it.
images.exact_structure: Left: 1 half roti filled teal #0072B2, the unit. Middle: 3 half rotis of exactly the same size in a row, filled teal #0072B2, with small grey #6B7280 plus signs between them. Right: 2 of those halves joined into 1 full round roti, filled amber #E69F00, and 1 teal half roti beside it. All halves exactly the same size. Exactly 1 unit half, 3 halves in the row, 1 full roti and 1 half.

images.takeaway: One half added three times is 3 × 1/2.
images.description: One half roti as the unit, three half rotis added as 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/2 = 3 × 1/2, and the same amount regrouped as 1 full roti and 1/2 more.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the halves in the middle row and say the amount as 3 times one half.

image_decisions.why: Half rotis laid out and regrouped show repeated addition of the unit one half in one picture.
